label: Correctness of the scoped epistemic judgment varies within the actual selective history
paraphrase: OPEN analyst premise, a within-history-variation reading, attribution deferred. Some scenario with the actual selective history differs from the actual scenario in whether the judged content is correct. This is not Street's no-relation horn: on pp. 121–122 (the Bermuda analogy) her horn holds the realist's truths fixed, lets the judgments vary with selective pressure, and reaches likely actual error through a coincidence step. A realism whose correctness is the same in every scenario, her paradigm target, fails this premise; the cross-history reading is encoded separately.
